# WebSocket Over TCP Instead of Geckos.io UDP

**Decision (2026-07-24, round 11):** replace geckos.io — UDP over WebRTC data channels — with plain
WebSocket over TCP (`ws`), across the whole of [[stickfps]].

**Driver: hosting cost, not technology.**

> "the original transport was geckos.io (**UDP-over-WebRTC**), which forces a UDP-capable host — and
> every managed host that does UDP (Fly.io, Oracle, the big clouds) requires a card. Swapped the whole
> transport to **plain WebSocket-over-TCP** (`ws`), which any persistent Node host can serve,
> including free no-card tiers (Render, Koyeb)."
> — browser_game_stickfps/PROGRESS.md, 2026-07-25

The trigger was a request to host the game online without a credit card. UDP was the only thing
requiring a card-gated host, so the transport was the cheapest constraint to remove.

## The old transport worked

This is the part that would be easy to get wrong in hindsight. Confirmed at interview:

> "Cost only — it worked fine."
> — interview, 2026-07-28

There was **no reliability problem, no browser-support problem and no debuggability problem** with
UDP-over-WebRTC. Nothing in the transport failed. This was a clean cost-driven trade, and reading a
technical failure into it would invent a rationale that does not exist.

## What was traded away

TCP gives ordered, reliable delivery — so a lost packet blocks every packet behind it until it is
retransmitted. For a 60 Hz position stream that is the wrong guarantee: the next snapshot makes the
lost one irrelevant, and waiting for it costs latency. Named and accepted as "unnoticeable at hobby
scale", which is a defensible call for a friends-and-bots game and would not be for a competitive
one. [[entity-interpolation]]'s 100 ms buffer absorbs more of this than it otherwise would.

## Why the swap was affordable

A `NetChannel` / `NetServer` abstraction was written to mirror **only the slice of the geckos.io API
the code actually used**. `geckosServer.ts` and `geckosClient.ts` were deleted and **no gameplay code
changed** — the authority model in [[server-authoritative-netcode]] never saw the transport. See
[[ws-websocket-server]] for what replaced it.

## Consequences

- Unblocked [[render-over-fly-io]] — Render had been rejected earlier *specifically* for having no
  public inbound UDP, and that objection died with this change.
- Left drift behind: `EXPOSE 10000/udp` in the [[docker]] image, `TASKS.md` step 8.1 still saying
  "UDP enabled", all four `.tooling` agent files still naming Geckos.io, and the SRS diagrams
  unchanged. See [[documentation-drift]].
